title: Low-Rank Tensor Decomposition for Key-Value Cache Compression in Large Language Models
outcome: Near-lossless 2x to 3x KV cache compression with accuracy within 2 percentage points of the uncompressed model
summary: For my registered MSc thesis at Universitaet Trier, I am developing JoLT for memory-efficient LLM inference. It combines partial Tucker decomposition with a compact low-bit correction term (a rotated residual) and an optimization step (Lagrangian budget allocation) that decides how much to compress each part of the cache under a fixed memory budget. The related preprint is A JoLT for the KV Cache: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.12550.
detail: KV caches can become a major memory cost during long-context LLM inference. In my thesis, I combine partial Tucker decomposition, a low-rank factorization over token and feature modes, with a rotated low-bit residual that cheaply corrects the approximation.

I use a Lagrangian dual to jointly choose the compression settings (decomposition ranks and residual bit widths) under a storage budget. Across five models and four model families, JoLT achieved near-lossless 2x to 3x compression while keeping accuracy within 2 percentage points of the uncompressed model. I evaluated it on 64K long-context retrieval and GSM8K reasoning.

title: RAG Resume API
outcome: Powers the live AI Q&A assistant embedded in this portfolio site
summary: I built a RAG API over my resume and project documents, using hybrid BM25 and local vector retrieval with cross-encoder reranking. I deployed the LlamaIndex and FastAPI service in Docker on Google Cloud Run.
detail: I indexed my resume and project documents so portfolio visitors can ask natural-language questions about my background, projects, and experience.

I used LlamaIndex with local ONNX BGE embeddings, hybrid BM25 and vector retrieval, and a local cross-encoder reranker. A free OpenRouter model produces context-aware answers without a paid embedding API.

I deployed the FastAPI backend in Docker on Google Cloud Run's free tier. I added per-IP rate limiting, an in-memory query cache, token streaming, and Google Sheets request logging for the public endpoint. The service powers the live Q&A assistant on this site.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Narrative Similarity (HeteroGNN + Text Fusion)
outcome: 72.5% pairwise accuracy and 95% precision on 500 story-comparison test cases spanning five languages
summary: I built a neuro-symbolic narrative-similarity system that combines a HeteroGNN over LLM-extracted story structure with Gemini text embeddings. I evaluated the interpretable additive fusion on pairwise and five-language cross-lingual data.
detail: I used GPT-OSS 20B to extract themes, actions, outcomes, and plot type into schema-validated JSON, then formed a heterogeneous graph with four node types. I combined the graph representation with Gemini text embeddings through a simple weighted average.

The system reached 72.5% accuracy on pairwise narrative similarity and 95% precision on 500 story-comparison test cases from the Tell-Me-Again dataset, spanning German, English, Spanish, French, and Italian. An angle analysis showed the graph and text signals carry largely independent information, so each one's contribution to the final similarity score can be measured exactly. I trained the GNN on 1,900 synthetic triplets, so generalization to substantially different narrative domains remains untested.

title: FEAR - Asymmetric RLVR for LLM Calibration and Abstention
outcome: At 1.5B and 3B, asymmetric rewards shifted abstention but did not improve calibration
summary: I tested whether asymmetric rewards in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) improve how well an LLM's confidence matches reality (calibration) and when it declines to answer (abstention). My GRPO training and evaluation pipeline on Qwen 2.5 found no calibration benefit at the tested scales, but produced a mechanistic explanation for why.
detail: I tested whether heavily penalizing wrong answers would make Qwen 2.5 models better calibrated or more willing to abstain. I trained seven reward conditions at 1.5B and the most promising reward settings at 3B across six math and general-reasoning benchmarks, using calibration and selective-prediction metrics.

I found that asymmetric rewards changed how often models abstained, not calibration or accuracy when answering. The reason: because of how GRPO normalizes rewards, penalty tuning only shifts the point at which the model declines to answer. It cannot change how confident the model is on individual questions.

I limited the conclusions to 1.5B and 3B Qwen 2.5 models. I did not run a 7B confirmation because of compute constraints, collected only partial multi-seed error bars, and did not run some planned follow-up analyses at scale.

title: Amazon Electronics Recommender System
outcome: Two-Tower MLP reached NDCG@10 of 0.3342, up from 0.3051 for the baseline, with sub-100ms CPU inference
summary: I built an end-to-end recommender on a 390,757-interaction Amazon Electronics sample. My Two-Tower MLP combines collaborative, metadata, and SBERT title signals, with FAISS candidate retrieval and MLP reranking in a FastAPI service on Azure Container Apps.
detail: I developed the system on an Amazon Reviews 2023 Electronics sample of 41,909 users, 136,934 items, and 390,757 interactions. I compared collaborative filtering with metadata and SBERT text-based models before selecting a Two-Tower MLP.

My best model reached NDCG@10 of 0.3342 versus 0.3051 for the collaborative-filtering baseline, a 9.5% relative gain, with paired t-tests across five seeds. I used FAISS to retrieve candidates from item embeddings and the full MLP to rerank them using metadata and text features.

I bundled the inference assets in one checkpoint, reducing startup time from 30 to 45 seconds to 2 to 3 seconds. I deployed the FastAPI service on Azure Container Apps with sub-100ms CPU inference after warm start. The current model does not handle new users or items with no interaction history.

title: Reflective CoT Faithfulness Study (Think Twice)
outcome: Reflective CoT reduced bias susceptibility by about 7 percentage points over standard CoT across 650 cases
summary: I co-built a team research study evaluating whether reflective chain-of-thought improves LLM reasoning faithfulness under controlled prompt bias.
detail: I co-built a reproducible Python evaluation across Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite and LLaMA 3.2 3B, comparing direct answering, chain-of-thought, and reflective chain-of-thought across 13 BIG-Bench Hard categories in zero-shot and few-shot settings.

We found that Reflective CoT reduced bias susceptibility by about 7 percentage points over standard CoT, but models still produced plausible rationales that did not reveal the prompt cue driving biased answers. Our results show that structured reflection improved bias resistance but did not establish faithful reasoning.

title: Risk-Averse Optimization (CVaR across 3 Domains)
outcome: When the controller's temperature model was badly wrong, CVaR control cut constraint violations from 100% of scenarios to 0%
summary: I applied CVaR-based risk-averse optimization to nonlinear programming, perturbed SVM classification, and wine-fermentation model predictive control.
detail: I implemented Conditional Value at Risk (CVaR) objectives, which optimize for the worst-case tail of outcomes, and tested them on three problems: a noisy benchmark function, an SVM trained on perturbed data, and a wine-fermentation controller.
In my open-loop fermentation comparison with severe temperature mismatch, the CVaR controller reduced the violation rate from 100% to 0%, while using more control effort.

In a separate closed-loop 21-day hot-scenario simulation, I found that CVaR improved final sugar and ethanol outcomes at higher control cost. This result is distinct from the open-loop violation comparison.

title: University Machine Learning Competitions (Top-3 in Three Challenges)
outcome: Top-3 finish in all three university Kaggle challenges
summary: I placed in the top three in three course-integrated Kaggle competitions spanning tabular machine learning, a PyTorch CNN trained from scratch, and few-shot LLM classification.
detail: I completed three University of Trier course competitions with reproducible single-file Python submissions.
I built a HistGradientBoostingClassifier with temporal and fare-derived features for taxi-tip prediction.
I designed a VGG-style PyTorch CNN trained from scratch with augmentation, AdamW, cosine learning-rate scheduling, and early stopping.
I built a few-shot classification workflow with 4-bit Gemma-3-12B inference and retrieval of similar training examples.

title: Transformer-Based Sentiment Analysis (YouTube Comments)
outcome: F1 = 0.81 on 10,000+ imbalanced YouTube comments, CI/CD to Docker Hub
summary: I fine-tuned BERT for YouTube-comment sentiment classification, served it through a Flask API, containerized it with Docker, and automated image publishing with GitHub Actions.
detail: I fine-tuned BERT with PyTorch and Hugging Face on an imbalanced dataset of more than 10,000 YouTube comments.

I reached an F1 score of 0.81, exposed the model through a Flask REST API, and published repeatable Docker images through GitHub Actions. I also deployed an interactive Gradio demo on Hugging Face Spaces.

title: Glaucoma Detection from Retinal Fundus Images
outcome: ICCSP 2020 paper reporting 86% F1 for SVM-based glaucoma classification
summary: I co-authored undergraduate work on glaucoma screening from retinal fundus images using optic-disc and optic-cup segmentation, cup-to-disc ratio measurement, and SVM classification.
detail: We developed an image-processing pipeline with threshold-based optic-disc segmentation and modified region growing for optic-cup segmentation, followed by cup-to-disc ratio measurement and SVM classification.
On the Drishti-GS dataset, we reported an F1 score of 86% for classification. We presented the work at ICCSP 2020 and published it on IEEE Xplore.
